name: CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark
description: The Center for Internet Security (CIS) Foundations Benchmark for Microsoft Azure provides prescriptive guidance for configuring Azure services securely. Covers IAM, storage, SQL, networking, and logging.

controls.title: Ensure Azure Storage accounts are not publicly accessible
controls.description: Storage accounts must restrict public network access. Public blob containers can expose sensitive data to the internet.
controls.rationale: Publicly accessible storage accounts have been repeatedly exploited in breaches. Azure Storage should use private endpoints or network rules, with public access disabled at the account level.
controls.query: MATCH (i:AzureStorage) WHERE i.public = true RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, 'AzureStorage' AS resourceType, i.region AS evidence

remediation.summary: Disable public network access on the storage account.
steps: Open the storage account in Azure Portal
Networking → set 'Public network access' to 'Disabled' or 'Enabled from selected networks'
Configure private endpoints for application access
Review and restrict container-level access policies
Enable storage account diagnostic logs

controls.title: Ensure Azure SQL Server does not allow public network access
controls.description: Azure SQL Servers must have 'publicNetworkAccess' disabled and use private endpoints or service endpoints for application access.
controls.rationale: Publicly accessible SQL servers are attack magnets. Disabling public network access and requiring private connectivity is a CIS Azure Level 1 control.
controls.query: MATCH (i:AzureSQLServer) WHERE i.public = true OR toLower(coalesce(i.publicNetworkAccess, '')) = 'enabled' RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, 'AzureSQLServer' AS resourceType, i.region AS evidence

remediation.summary: Disable public network access on the SQL server.
steps: Open the SQL server in Azure Portal
Networking → Public network access → set to 'Disabled'
Configure private endpoint for application access
Add the application's subnet to the virtual network rules if service endpoints are used
Audit firewall rules and remove any 0.0.0.0 allow entries

controls.title: Ensure Azure SQL Server enforces minimum TLS version 1.2
controls.description: Azure SQL Servers must reject connections using TLS versions below 1.2.
controls.rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 have known vulnerabilities. CIS and NIST SP 800-52 require TLS 1.2 or higher for data in transit.
controls.query: MATCH (i:AzureSQLServer) WHERE i.minimalTlsVersion IS NOT NULL AND i.minimalTlsVersion < '1.2' RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, 'AzureSQLServer' AS resourceType, i.minimalTlsVersion AS evidence

remediation.summary: Set the SQL server minimum TLS version to 1.2.
steps: Open the SQL server in Azure Portal
Security → Firewalls and virtual networks → set Minimum TLS version to 1.2
Verify application clients support TLS 1.2 before applying
Update connection strings if needed

controls.title: Ensure Azure App Service enforces HTTPS only
controls.description: App Services must have 'HTTPS Only' enabled so HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.
controls.rationale: Serving content over HTTP exposes session tokens and sensitive data to network interception. CIS requires encryption in transit for all application traffic.
controls.query: MATCH (i:AzureAppService) WHERE coalesce(i.httpsOnly, 'false') = 'false' RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, 'AzureAppService' AS resourceType, coalesce(i.httpsOnly, 'not set') AS evidence

remediation.summary: Enable HTTPS Only on the App Service.
steps: Open the App Service in Azure Portal
Configuration → General settings → toggle HTTPS Only to On
Bind a TLS certificate (App Service Managed Certificate or custom)
Test the application over HTTPS
Update DNS and any downstream callers if they use HTTP URLs

controls.title: Ensure Azure VMs are not directly internet-facing without a load balancer
controls.description: Azure Virtual Machines should not have a public IP directly attached. Use a load balancer, application gateway, or bastion for access.
controls.rationale: Directly-exposed VMs bypass centralised access controls, WAF protection, and logging. This is a common cause of ransomware entry via RDP/SSH brute force.
controls.query: MATCH (i:AzureVM) WHERE i.public = true RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, 'AzureVM' AS resourceType, i.region AS evidence

remediation.summary: Remove the public IP and front the VM with a load balancer or Azure Bastion.
steps: Identify the public IP attached to the VM
Provision an Azure Load Balancer or Application Gateway
Update DNS to point to the load balancer
Detach the public IP from the VM
Use Azure Bastion for administrative access instead of public RDP/SSH

controls.title: Ensure Azure Redis caches require TLS (non-SSL port disabled)
controls.description: Azure Cache for Redis must not have the non-SSL port enabled. All connections must use TLS.
controls.rationale: Cache data often contains session tokens, API keys, and sensitive query results. Unencrypted Redis ports expose this data to network-level attackers.
controls.query: MATCH (i:AzureRedis) WHERE toLower(coalesce(i.enableNonSslPort, 'false')) = 'true' RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, 'AzureRedis' AS resourceType, 'Non-SSL port enabled' AS evidence

remediation.summary: Disable the non-SSL port on the Redis cache.
steps: Open the Redis cache in Azure Portal
Advanced settings → toggle 'Allow access only via SSL' to On
Verify clients are using the SSL port (6380) and update connection strings
Ensure minimum TLS version is 1.2
